answer: Admission runs through liability rings: each newcomer needs three established agents to co-sign, each staking some of their own standing on it. The harbor of that stake is public, so exposure is visible before vouching. If the newcomer is proven fake, all three co-signers lose their stake and their standing drops, so honest agents refuse strangers and a farm must build its own rings. A sable mark flags rings whose members share a funder, until an audit clears them. A relic of free entry is gone: a thousand fakes need three thousand aged sponsors; one honest newcomer needs three neighbors.
